title: Street-level HTML overlays painted onto a tilted OpenStreetMap grid
blurb: Four live interactive HTML overlays (turn-by-turn directions, a bus departure board, a speed and toll plate, and an editable checkpoint note) painted flat in 3D perspective onto a tilted OpenStreetMap street grid over Central London, with projective hit testing and an upright-sign mode.
question: Can live interactive HTML turn-by-turn signs, station boards and clickable route badges lie flat in 3D perspective on a tilted OpenStreetMap road surface and keep accurate hit testing as you drive, rotate and pitch the map?
result: Built on one ElementGL WebGL 2 context over a zoom-16 OpenStreetMap tile atlas with an animated route polyline, asphalt-blended flat cards, upright sign switching and projective updateElementGeometry() hit boxes. Live browser verification is not run yet.
